subject: Concession structuring and runtime compatibility mapping
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@nimbushealth.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: Luis Carvalho <luis.carvalho@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Evaluation follow-up — economics + runtime questions

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency profile looked promising for our primary inference paths. As we start the procurement loop I wanted to flag two things that are blocking a straight replacement:

1) Economics: Our procurement team is asking whether Redwood can match the effective unit economics we have with our current vendor when we normalize for 95th percentile latency and embedding throughput. We know list price parity is unlikely, but they asked for a concrete concession framework (credits, staged discounts, or commit pricing) we can show to leadership.

2) Runtime compatibility: Our platform relies heavily on preserving KV cache across warm restarts and using a custom quantization layer in a couple of internal models. The evaluation used a small sample; we need a short technical mapping that explains which of our model variations are fully supported without rework and where we should expect refactor effort (KV cache migration, quantized operator differences, performance delta estimate).

Can you share a single package that combines an economic concession and a technical compatibility mapping? That will help us decide whether to proceed with a pilot or ask the current vendor for an acceptable counter-offer.

If useful, I can share a brief inventory of the top 12 models (names + token distribution) — Luis is looping to keep the fast followers in the procurement path in the loop.

Best,
Maya
Director, Cloud Platform
NimbusHealth

Attachments: nimbus-eval-notes.pdf (summary, 1 page)
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Luis Carvalho <luis.carvalho@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluation follow-up — economics + runtime questions

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear ask. Really appreciate the model inventory offer; that will speed the mapping.

High-level proposal:
- Concession structure: a 3-month onboarding credit that offsets up to 30% of estimated token spend for the pilot window, plus a 12-month staged commitment tier (details to follow from contracts).
- Technical mapping: Rishi (cc'd) will produce a short compatibility matrix showing (a) models we can run without code changes, (b) models requiring small operator remaps, and (c) models that will need refactors for the quantization layer. We'll include estimated engineering effort and expected latency delta for each.

Next steps I propose:
1) Rishi to deliver the compatibility matrix and a short ops play for KV cache migration by EOD Friday.
2) I will draft an internal concession term sheet and send a DocuSign-ready offer for your procurement and legal to review next week.

Would Nimbus prefer credits or an upfront one-time onboarding credit + discounted months? We can structure either, but procurement often prefers an explicit dollar credit to show on P&L.

Thanks — looping Rishi and Laura for inputs.

Best,
Olga
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: Evaluation follow-up — economics + runtime questions

Internal — forwarding Nimbus ask. Quick notes inline: they want a combined econ + tech package for a potential vendor replacement. Key asks: preserve KV cache behavior and support our custom quantization with minimal refactor.

Luis (external) copied the inventory; Maya says she'll share top-12 soon. Can you prioritize a compact matrix (1 sheet) with:
- Model name
- Token distribution (rough)
- Category: direct-run | operator-remap | requires-refactor
- Estimated eng hours to remediate (S/M/L)
- Expected P50/P95 latency delta

Rishi — can you also include whether we can offer a temporary runtime shim (container-level wrapper) that preserves the KV prefix semantics for ~90% of cases (even if slower) so Nimbus has an escape hatch during migration?

Laura — will need your input on realistic credit sizing (we need a number procurement can present).

Cheers,
Olga
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 23 Oct 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Fwd: Evaluation follow-up — economics + runtime questions

Hi team — ran the initial mapping against the inventory Maya provided (thanks). Summary highlights below; I attached the CSV with the matrix and microbench numbers.

Quick summary (high level):
- 5 models: direct-run. No code changes; KV cache semantics preserved. Expect p50 latency within +/- 5%, p95 within +8% in our hosted config.
- 4 models: operator-remap. These use a custom quantize/dequantize op. We can provide a compatibility layer mapping most ops; expect a small accuracy risk in the tails and p95 latency +12–18%. Estimated remediation: 1–2 engineer-weeks each (S/M).
- 3 models: refactor needed. These depend on a proprietary quantization flow and in-place KV mutation patterns. Refactor estimate: 3–6 engineer-weeks per model (L).

Technical escape-hatches:
- Runtime shim: feasible. We can wrap requests in a compatibility layer that preserves KV naming and replay semantics. Tradeoffs: adds ~30–45ms overhead and removes some batching efficiency; recommended as a short-term migration assist only.
- Quantization advice: we can offer a suggested quantization profile that closely matches their internal operator but requires recompiles — typically +5–10% latency vs their current optimized path, but with large token-cost savings.

Deliverables included: runtime-compatibility-matrix.csv (model-by-model), microbench-report.pdf (latency/throughput traces).

Recommendation for offer packaging:
- Pilot window: 3 months (up to 12M tokens/month) on hosted with a 25% onboarding credit applied to invoices for the pilot period.
- Migration support: 40 professional services hours (SE-assisted) included; additional hours at standard PS rates.
- Technical SLA: p95 latency SLO and rollback plan.

I can produce a slightly lower-overhead shim if we take a short audit window to pin the worst offending operator implementations.

—Rishi

Attachment: runtime-compatibility-matrix.csv (model mapping), microbench-report.pdf (3 pages)
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, Maya Singh <maya.singh@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Luis Carvalho <luis.carvalho@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluation follow-up — economics + runtime questions

Hi Maya,

Thanks for the patient turnaround while we scoped the technical work. Based on Rishi's matrix and standard deal guidance, here's a concrete offer Nimbus can take to procurement: 

1) Financial concession (pilot):
- 25% credit applied to billed token spend for the first 3 months of the pilot (applies to invoices up to a cap equivalent to 12M tokens/month).
- One-time onboarding credit: $45,000 to offset migration tooling and early egress costs (appears as a line-item credit).

2) Technical & operational support:
- 40 hours of PS for migration assistance (included). Additional hours at our published PS rate.
- Runtime shim available for the pilot to preserve KV semantics (adds ~30–45ms overhead; recommended only for high-risk models).
- A short performance audit (2 engineer-days) to identify the top operator hotspots and reduce shim impact.

3) Terms / cadence:
- Pilot term: 3 months. If Nimbus converts to a 12-month committed tier within 30 days of pilot end, we will apply an additional 10% credit to the first committed quarter.
- Offer is contingent on mutual NDA/terms; we will share a DocuSign offer and a short SOW for PS hours.

I've attached a DocuSign-ready term sheet and the line-item structure. If this package looks good, we can turn a preliminary DocuSign in ~48 hours and schedule the audit session.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Renewals | Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-offer_term_sheet.pdf (DocuSign-ready)

Laura / Olga — this looks usable. Procurement asked for the explicit dollar credit shown (thanks) and wants the DocuSign link for legal redlines. Two quick Qs before we move to contract: 

1) Can the onboarding credit be drawn down against PS hours if Nimbus chooses to use Redwood's engineering team beyond the included 40 hours? Procurement prefers flexibility rather than separate invoices.
2) For the pilot cap (12M tokens/month) — what is the true overage rate if we spike above during the pilot? We need a clear, simple number to keep in the SOW.

If you can update the term sheet with those two items I can push this to legal and get back with requested redlines by next Wed. Otherwise, we can accept in principle and start scheduling the audit session.

Thanks —
Maya
